title: Quantized concurrency race causing intermittent unsupported-op crashes and embedding drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Incident summary: Between 2026-03-08 22:30 and 2026-03-09 03:45 UTC, a subset of quantized model deployments experienced intermittent crash loops and silent accuracy drift for embedding and reranking workloads. Root cause appears to be a concurrency race between the quantized kernel selector and the VM-level op canonicalizer that produced a transient opsig variant not covered by the quantized operator table. This led to fallback to an unsupported op path which triggered memory corruption on some GPU configs and a small but measurable embedding distribution shift in production canaries. This ticket captures post-incident action items, owners, and milestones to eliminate the race, tighten canary coverage, and add guardrails to prevent silent drift.
impact: ~1.6% of production requests for small-batch embedding endpoints experienced elevated error rates and 0.7% of in-flight inference returned embeddings with shifted L2 norms triggering downstream rerank regressions. Multiple customer tenants on dedicated pools saw retry storms and latency spikes. No data leakage or exfiltration was detected.
timeline_notes: 2026-03-08 22:27 UTC: Canary alert - quantized-embed-canary failed threshold for L2-norm deviation (auto-alert)
2026-03-08 22:35 UTC: SRE paged. Initial mitigation: scaled affected Dedicated pools down to single-concurrency mode for suspect nodes.
2026-03-09 00:10 UTC: Engineering confirmed correlation with recent kernel-selector rollout (runtime-1.22-canary).
2026-03-09 01:45 UTC: Hotfix: temporarily pinned quant-kernel-index to legacy selector on 4 affected nodes; crash loops stopped but drift persisted for requests already cached.
2026-03-09 02:30 UTC: Rollback of runtime-1.22-canary to previous selector version across canary region.
2026-03-09 03:00 UTC: Post-rollback validation: canary L2-norm deviation returned to baseline; production throttles removed.
root_cause: A race between the kernel selector (which assigns quantized operator variants) and the op canonicalizer that rewrites op signatures under high concurrency. Under certain timing windows a newly-canonicalized op signature reached the runtime after the kernel index snapshot was taken, producing a mismatch: the kernel index did not contain a compatible quantized op mapping for the revised opsig, causing the runtime to fall back to an unsupported operator code path that is not memory-safety vetted for the quantized tensor formats on some GPU drivers.
mitigation_taken: Pinned kernel-selector version in canaries and queued an immediate rollback of the canary rollout.
Scoped Dedicated pools to single concurrency for suspect nodes to reduce race surface while rollback propagated.
Added emergency canary alert to detect L2-norm deviation for top embedding endpoints and rerank metrics to shorten time-to-detect.
long_term_action_items: (A1) Implement atomic kernel-index swap: ensure kernel selector updates publish a new index atomically and block dispatch until index consistency is observed. Owner: Marcus Nguyen. Due: 2026-03-18.

(A2) Add opsig-version pinning metadata to model manifests so a serving slice can validate compatibility at load-time instead of relying on eventual selector convergence. Owner: Priya Rao. Due: 2026-04-01.

(A3) Expand canary evaluation to include distributional checks (L2 norm, cosine similarity drift) for embeddings, with synthetic stability probes on each rollout. Owner: Eval Squad (lead: Hector Gomez). Due: 2026-03-25.

(A4) Enhance fallback path safety: implement a guarded fallback that validates tensor layout and uses a safe (slower) demotion path rather than executing unvetted code. Owner: Runtime Core (lead: Lin Wei). Due: 2026-04-05.
(A5) Add telemetry: opsig->kernel mapping mismatches should emit high-cardinality trace events and a specific alert when mismatch rate > 0.1% of requests. Owner: Telemetry Team. Due: 2026-03-15.
(A6) Nightly randomized stress test: run high-concurrency quantized op canonicalization races in CI with reproducibility harness. Owner: CI Team. Due: 2026-03-22.
(A7) Postmortem knowledge transfer: run a runbook review with SRE and platform teams and add an incident playbook for quantized-opset instability. Owner: Aisha Patel. Due: 2026-03-16.
short_term_workplan: 1) Complete canary rollback verification across regions and ensure no stale kernel-index snapshots remain (SRE, 2026-03-12).
2) Patch emergency telemetry to surface opsig/kernel mismatch metrics and deploy to canaries (Telemetry, 2026-03-13).
3) Deploy guarded fallback hotfix behind feature-flag to a small set of canary nodes (Runtime Core, 2026-03-14).
open_risks: Delayed implementation of atomic kernel-index swap could leave a narrow window where future rollouts produce similar mismatches under bursty load.
Fallback demotion may introduce measurable latency increase for affected requests; need SLO review and customer comms plan.
Edge GPU drivers that exhibited memory-safety failures may still trigger rare crash modes; additional hardware-specific tests required.
decisions: Do not revert quantization support universally; instead adopt targeted guardrails and atomic publishing for kernel indices.
Prioritize telemetry and canary expansion before further kernel-selector rollouts.
Require opsig compatibility tests in PR pipeline for kernel-selector and op canonicalizer changes.

resolution_criteria: Atomic kernel-index publishing implemented and validated in canaries with zero opsig/kernel mismatch alerts for 72 hours.
Guarded fallback deployed to 90% of nodes with telemetry showing safe demotion paths exercising at least once per load scenario.
Canary distributional checks detect any embedding L2-norm deviation > 0.5% within 5 minutes of rollout and block promotion automatically.
